summary.headline: Exide Q1 FY27 standalone revenue grew 17.6% and EBITDA rose 19.5% to INR655 crores, with margin at 12.4%.
summary.overview: Management reported broad-based double-digit growth across automotive OEM, replacement, home inverter, solar, industrial and exports, helped by a strong summer and a low base. EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps YoY and about 70 bps QoQ despite higher input costs from West Asia disruption and rupee weakness. Price increases of 4-6% YoY across categories were taken, with further hikes to be decided case by case. In lithium-ion, all four Bangalore lines are installed, the NCM cylindrical and LFP prismatic lines have started customer samples, and revenue is expected to start during FY27. Management declined to give full-year guidance.

segments.name: Automotive OEM
segments.commentary: Grew about 25% YoY for a third straight quarter; 4W OEM volume up 21% and 2W OEM up 20%, on a low base. Management expects percentage growth to slow in H2 against a strong Q3/Q4 FY26.

segments.name: Replacement (2W/4W)
segments.commentary: 4-wheeler replacement volume grew about 10%; all replacement businesses reported double-digit revenue growth.

segments.name: Home inverters and solar
segments.commentary: Both grew over 20% YoY on summer demand; solar volume grew about 12-14% and solar posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR400+ crores. Inverters are 15-25% of revenue depending on season.

segments.name: Industrial infrastructure (ex-telecom)
segments.commentary: Maintained double-digit growth, supported by industrial UPS and traction. Government tenders were muted in the quarter, with an H2 pick-up expected.

segments.name: Lithium-ion (Exide Energy Solutions)
segments.commentary: Bangalore plant: 4 lines installed; NCM cylindrical and LFP prismatic lines are shipping samples. Lithium pack business is small (INR100-200 crores in FY26 per management) and management does not expect it to be profitable with imported cells.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 revenue guidance; management cited poor visibility on market and H2 base effects, though Q2 benefits from a low base.
Bangalore plant revenue expected to commence during FY27 shortly; utilisation of 25-30% of the factory in the first year, which management reaffirmed.
FY27 lithium-ion capex approved by Board at INR1,400 crores, with INR100 crores spent in July; may be reviewed.
Phase 1 (6 GWh) has no PLI support; Phase 2 capex is lower than Phase 1 as land and utilities for 12 GWh are already built, but total could exceed the earlier INR7,000 crore plan.
Target of 50-60% localisation of lithium-ion bill of materials in 2-3 years.
Q2 price increases not yet decided; will be taken in small steps as input costs move.
capex_capacity: Bangalore giga factory: equipment for all 4 lines delivered and installed; utilities fully operational.

First NCM cylindrical line began customer sample deliveries in Q1; LFP prismatic line has started samples for 3W and telecom. Lines 1 and 3 are the first to be run; Line 4 (LFP, for 4W OEMs) is to be commissioned around end of FY27.
Phase 1 capacity is 6 GWh, with provision to expand to 12 GWh in the next few years. Pack capacity in-house is 1.5 GWh.

Lead-acid: INR500 crores is set aside every year for the core business, for bottleneck debottlenecking, automation and capacity expansion, mainly in 4W. Exide has 5 SLI plants with brownfield headroom.
Pilot line for R&D expected at end of calendar 2026; more than 100 R&D engineers are in Bangalore.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was double-digit in most businesses: 4W replacement about 10%, 4W OEM 21%, 2W OEM 20%, solar 12-14%.
Price increases of 4-6% YoY were taken across categories. Management expects to take further 1-2% steps as needed.
Input costs were elevated due to West Asia disruption and rupee weakness, while LME lead in USD was range-bound.
Management said 2W/3W/telecom lithium demand is a switch from imported cells, not new demand, and that the 3W market is about 70-75% aftermarket retrofits.

Chinese export VAT rebate on cells fell from 9% to 6%, and management expects the removal from 1 January 2027 to affect imported-cell landed costs. China export controls on raw materials are deferred to around November.

qa_highlights.question: Split of volume vs pricing growth, and whether any new contracts contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was double-digit in most businesses (4W OEM 21%, 2W OEM 20%, 4W replacement 10%, solar 12-14%). Price correction added to top-line growth. No new contract wins contributed.

qa_highlights.question: Can full-year FY27 growth of 15-16% be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no full-year guidance. It flagged H2 percentage slowdown in auto OEM due to the high base from Q3/Q4 FY26, though absolute volumes remain high (passenger vehicles up from 1.2 to 1.4 million).

qa_highlights.question: Cell yields and early learnings from the giga factory?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields are improving, but the real yield will only be visible at 3-shift operation. Management did not disclose yield numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Are there PLI and pricing views for the imported-cell competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating the 10 GWh PLI re-application. It declined to comment on early-phase margins, citing the China VAT rebate removal from 1 January as a watch item.

qa_highlights.question: Inverter share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Home inverters are 15-25% of revenue, depending on the season.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of 2W EV OEM and 4W OEM engagement?
qa_highlights.answer: Talks are under way with about 3 major 2W OEMs (about 80% of EV volume) and homologation is in progress. For 4W, 1-2 major OEMs are in talks, with Line 4 expected to be commissioned around end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 lithium-ion capex and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: INR1,400 crores is approved for FY27 (INR100 crores spent in July). Phase 1 is 6 GWh, expandable to 12 GWh; management declined to give rupee revenue figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25-30% utilisation target achievable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed 25-30% factory utilisation for the first year and declined to forecast FY27 revenue, citing contractual BESS delivery dates and start-up timing.
